subject: Air-gapped Private deployment — HW, upgrades & ops clarifications
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novalabs.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -0000
Subject: Air-gapped Private deployment — HW, upgrades & ops clarifications

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you and Samuel. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on the right deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private on-prem):

Recap:
- Novalabs prefers a fully air-gapped Private deployment (no outbound internet from the appliance).
- Primary use is internal search + code-assist for R&D (steady token volumes, occasional heavy batches).
- Compliance requirement: quarterly penetration tests and annual SOC2 review.

Immediate clarification items (helps us size hardware and ops plan):
1) Rack / power constraints: can you confirm standard rack units available (U), available PDUs (208V vs 120V), and max per-rack power draw?
2) Upgrade cadence: do you want Redwood-managed offline upgrade packages (we deliver an installable bundle + ops MOP) or will your infra team run upgrades? If you want Redwood to perform the upgrade we need a standard maintenance window and physical access SLA.
3) Spares and firmware: do you have an existing spares pool for GPU nodes/PSUs? If not, would you prefer Redwood supply a small spares kit under a service addendum?
4) Network / data egress policy: confirm whether we can use a temporary jumpbox for image transfer during install or if only USB-transfer of bundles is allowed.

Next steps I propose:
- Can we get the site rack diagram and power table (very helpful for final BOM)?
- I’ll loop Rishi (runtime lead) and Marissa (ops/installation) for a short technical walkthrough.
- If procurement is ready, Samuel — we can share a draft SOW and order path after the BOM.

Attachments: please attach the rack diagram if available — that will speed things up.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first platform for predictable LLM inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novalabs.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Park <samuel.park@novalabs.io>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 18:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Air-gapped Private deployment — HW, upgrades & ops clarifications

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) Rack/power: We have two server rooms. Primary room is 42U racks, PDUs are 208V three-phase. Typical per-rack limit is 10kW. We’ll attach a rack diagram — see novalabs-site-rack-diagram.pdf.

2) Upgrades: Preference is for Redwood to provide an offline upgrade bundle and for our infra team to run the install. For major upgrades we may request Redwood-run upgrade support (we'll need a remote MOP first). Standard maintenance windows are Sat 0200–0600 local (PST).

3) Spares: We do not have GPU spare nodes on-site. We can keep a 1-node spare for critical failures but would prefer Redwood offer an optional spares kit for the first year.

4) Image transfer: Network policy is strict — we cannot allow outbound connections except via an approved, pre-provisioned transfer appliance. USB-only delivery is allowed but slower; jumpbox requires pre-approved firewall rules and paperwork.

Attaching: novalabs-site-rack-diagram.pdf, and a partially completed SOC2 answers workbook (NOVA-SOC2-answers.xlsx).

Happy to sync on a quick technical call. Samuel is looped for procurement notes.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Cloud Infrastructure, Novalabs
elena@novalabs.io

Elena —

Appreciate the fast response and the attachments — that covers a lot. Quick notes from our side and proposed schedule: 

Rishi: can you confirm the preferred GPU footprint for the workload described (search + code-assist) — estimated steady-state 30 tok/s with burst to 150 tok/s for nightly batches? We’ll start with an 8-GPU node profile for initial sizing unless you advise otherwise.

Marissa: ops ask — if Novalabs wants Redwood to hold a spares kit, we’ll need to draft a one-year spares SKUs + SLA (RTS 72h replacement shipping + on-site swap). Agree on weekend upgrade windows (Sat 02:00–06:00 PST) as proposed.

Proposal: Technical walkthrough with Novalabs infra team this week (45min). I can do Wed 27 Jan 14:00 PST or Thu 28 Jan 09:00 PST. Which works for you?

Action: Samuel — once we lock the slot, we can attach a draft SOW and preliminary BOM that ties to the rack diagram.

Best,
Kimberly

Thanks Kim/Elena — quick technical notes: 

- For the described profile I recommend baseline nodes with 8x A40-class GPUs (or equivalent Ampere family), 1TB RAM, NVMe cache for KV store. That gives headroom for batch/latency tradeoffs.
- If Novalabs cannot host spares, we should include a spare GPU board and spare PSU in the service kit.
- For offline upgrades we provide an installable bundle (signed) and a checklist MOP. If their policy only allows USB delivery, we will prepare a USB-signed bundle and pre-validate hashes over the call.

I can be on the technical walkthrough. Wed 27 Jan 14:00 PST works for me.
